To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. The African American Heritary Prostate Cancer ( AAHPC ) study has identified a number of genes that may contribute to prostate cancer in African Americans.
(i) The AAHPC study identified 77 families with at least 4 cases of prostate cancer, 5 of which had 2 or more cases with a diagnosis of prostate cancer at age ≤ 55 years.
the genetic architecture of prostate cancer is complex, with both common and rare variants contributing to disease susceptibility.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the genes responsible for prostate cancer susceptibility, the elucidation of their biological function in normal and malignant prostate epithelium, and the identification of the molecular events leading to prostate cancer.
the genetic epidemiology of hereditary prostate cancer (HPC), the genetic etiology of HPC, and the genetic epidemiology and genetic etiology of hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer (HNPCC).
understanding how genetic variation influences the development of prostate cancer in African‐American men and the development of prostate cancers that are more aggressive and lethal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the African American Herapeutic Prostate Cancer Study was a success in its efforts to identify the genetic factors contributing to prostate cancer in African American men.
the AAHPC Study is a large, well‐conducted and carefully documented study of African American families with early onset hereditary prostate cancer.
